newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek o/n spikes, bonds hold, FRNs down, ecu/drs flat.
newsitem.headline: Greek o/n spikes, bonds hold, FRNs down, ecu/drs flat.

text.p: The Greek overnight rate spiked up on tight liquidity conditions and long-term depos rose but forex forwards were little changed, dealers said.
Fixed coupon bonds were holding, FRNs were trading lower and ecu/drachma was ranging above the 309 level.
"The overnight rate has risen sharply on tight interbank liquidity," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank. "Long-term depos are also up but the forward curve is holding."
The market appears to be short drachmas right now but liquidity should balance out later on, the trader said.
Dealers said they expected the central bank to inject some cash on Wednesday when about 150 billion drachmas of 14-day funds mature.
The bond market was quiet with fixed coupon bonds holding late Monday levels but FRNs were down, dealers said.

"Fixed coupon bonds are little changed but we have seen some selling in FRNs with discount margins rising up to 78-80 basis points against Monday's 75 basis points," said a bond trader at a private bank.
But a bond dealer at a foreign bank said some foreign investors were expressing interest for FRNs at current prices.

"I think we will see buying interest from abroad for the seven-year floaters around current secondary market price levels," said a bond dealer at a foreign bank. "Liquidity might be tight right now but it will be boosted somehow in the next few days."
Greece will auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs on June 26.

The gross redemption yield of the benchmark 10-year coupon bond was steady at 9.11 percent, the five-year bond was yielding 9.74 percent from 9.72 percent late on Monday and the three-year bond an unchanged 10.15 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.76/86 from Monday's 157.880 fix, the dollar at 271.57/67 drachmas from 272.520 and the ecu at 309.12/22 from 309.250 drachmas.

"The market is basically frozen and ecu/drachma is trading around 315," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "If interbank rates stay where they are and the U.S. dollar gets stronger, the drachma will gain against the ecu and the mark."
The National Bank of Greece quoted the following early rates:
** Overnight at 12.10-12.60
** One week at 11.50-12.00
** Two weeks at 11.50-12.00
** Three weeks at 11.50-12.00
** One month at 11.50-12.00
** Two months at 11.40-11.90
** Three months at 11.40-11.90
** Six months at 10.90-11.40
** Nine months at 10.70-11.20
** Twelve months at 10.50-11.00
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
